tier_rationale: The manufacturer's own product page describes a motor-driven, sensor-regulated fountain (HydroSpin technology, automatic low-water shutoff, LED indicators) powered by USB with no WiFi, Bluetooth, or app mentioned anywhere. No FCC grant was found for the product, and this is a meaningful absence because the same vendor (Radio Systems Corporation, PetSafe's parent) does file FCC grants for its radio-equipped products, such as its pet containment fence transmitters — establishing that the vendor files when a radio is present and did not file here.
the_unplug_test: Nothing to unplug from a network — there isn't one. It plugs into a wall outlet or USB power for its circulation motor and water-level sensor, which shuts the pump off automatically when the reservoir runs low. It has no WiFi, no Bluetooth, no app, and nothing to lose if your internet goes down, because it was never connected to it.

repairability.notes: Filter cartridges are a routine consumable; the motor/sensor module was not confirmed as separately replaceable.

sources.supports: Manufacturer's own product page: 'Smart, quiet motor with sensors to regulate water flow, automatically shutting off at low levels' via patented HydroSpin technology, USB power, LED indicators; no WiFi, Bluetooth, or app mentioned anywhere on the page. Price $54.99 for the 60 oz (PWW00-17957); 90 oz and 128 oz variants also listed.

No FCC grant found for the Outlast Pet Fountain. Sibling control: the same grantee, Radio Systems Corporation (PetSafe's parent), holds multiple FCC grants for its radio-equipped products, e.g. pet containment fence transmitters (KBS050210, KBS050229, KBS050232, 9-14 kHz), establishing the vendor files when a radio exists and did not file for this product.

open_questions: Whether the motor/sensor board is separately replaceable if it fails was not confirmed from the product page — worth checking a teardown or the printed warranty terms.
notes: A useful counter-example inside the same vendor's lineup as PetSafe's WiFi-connected feeders and containment products: the fountain line was never given a connected variant to compare against, and the sibling FCC filings for the fence transmitters make the absence meaningful rather than just unproven.
